subject: How do you make functions to wrap up Shiny output$ objects?

messages.author: 1667ac6354bdba89
messages.subject: How do you make functions to wrap up Shiny output$ objects?
parts:
Hello there, again thanks for great product.

I'm working on a package that takes a lot of "boiler plate" Shiny input and output objects, and wraps them up in a function.  The idea is to sacrifice a bit of customisation for quick start apps.

For example:

renderAuthenticationMenu <- function(input, session){

    observe({

        foo <- input$foo

        choice <- df[blah == foo, ]

        updateSelectInput(session, "foo.id", label="foo", choices = choice)

    })

    observe({

        cow <- input$cow

        choice <- df[blah == cow, ]

        updateSelectInput(session, "cow.id", label="cow", choices = choice)

    })
    
}

This works great for input and session stuff, but it doesn't work when I do a wrapper around output objects.  I would like to also do similar with output - how can I get the output back out into the scope of the calling function?  If I try similar to above but with outputs, it can't find them in reactive functions later on in the the serverApp function.

Is it something to do with environments? (a bit out of my R comfort zone) parent.frame()?  Or do I need to make some return for the functions using reactiveValues() ?

Hope someone can help!

Yours sincerely,
Mark

messages.subject: Re: How do you make functions to wrap up Shiny output$ objects?
parts: Can you provide an example of what you mean by "output"? Do you literally mean plots and tables? Or do you mean arbitrary calculated values (reactive expressions)? I would've assumed you meant plots and tables but "it can't find them in reactive functions later on" seems to indicate you mean reactive expressions.

messages.subject: Re: How do you make functions to wrap up Shiny output$ objects?
parts:
Dear Joe,

Yes I mean reactive expressions - I see now that the output$blah stuff also renders ok.

But when I try to refer to reactive expressions, I get messages such as “not allowed outside a reactive environment”.

Here is an attempt at an example:

## function sourced or in package

AuthMenuMacro <- function(input, session, code){

  …other observe functions that update menus….

  …other output functions that output plots, data tables….
  
  AuthToken <- reactive({
    
    token <- getTokenFromCode(code)

  })

}

## server.r

code <- createAuthenticationCode()

shinyServer(function(input, output, session)){
  
  AuthMenuMacro(input, output, code)

  output$API_plot <- renderPlot({
 
    ## error as can’t see function AuthToken() within renderAuthMenu()
    data <- getAPIData(AuthToken())

    plot(data)

  }) 


}

So in server.r I have functions that call AuthToken().  This works fine when the AuthToken() is within the shinyServer call, but when trying to make this function so it can be called from a package, I get the errors.

I have tried using <<- and environments, but it doesn’t like that, also various combinations of reactiveValues(), but perhaps I haven’t got the syntax quite right. 

I can get kinda what I want if I just take the functions into a source file and source it locally in the shinyServer() function, but I’d like to see if this can be done via a function so it can be used in a package, and to be able to be neater calling variables etc to the functions within.

Perhaps this just isn’t a good idea, but its at least educational to ask :)

Yours sincerely,
Mark
